title: Composable adminlet layer for policy-gated runbook fragments
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a small, composable 'adminlet' primitive and authoring layer so runbooks can be expressed as sequences of typed, policy-gated fragments. Adminlets are lightweight, reusable operations (e.g., rotate-key, drain-worker, invalidate-cache, rehydrate-prefix) with a typed input schema, server-side validators, auditable execution metadata, and a dry-run simulation mode. The goal is to make on-call/first-line support safer and faster by giving playbook authors curated building blocks that enforce RBAC, parameter constraints, and telemetry by default. This ticket implements the core API, server-side policy enforcement, a basic dry-run harness, and a minimal Console authoring surface to compose and preview runbook fragments.
acceptance_criteria: Adminlet spec: JSON Schema manifest for each adminlet (name, version, inputs, outputs, required_policies) is persisted and queryable via API
Server-side policy engine evaluates required_policies against caller identity and returns explicit deny/allow decisions
Dry-run mode simulates adminlet execution and returns structured 'intended changes' without mutating state
Execution records create an immutable audit entry with correlation_id, parameters (redacted as required), outcome, and links to logs
Console composer shows typed inputs, validates client-side using the adminlet schema, and offers a preview/dry-run button
Feature flag gated rollout: behind feature flag 'adminlets.composable' and enabled for internal teams only by default

Found two validation failure modes we need to support: synchronous server validation and async cross-service checks.

2026-03-12 - Arjun Patel: Addressed secret redaction and put encryption-at-rest task into ENG-276547. Added correlation_id tracing across orchestration and logs. Started wiring telemetry schema: adminlet.name, adminlet.version, user.id, policy_evaluation.result, dry_run=true/false, duration_ms.

2026-03-14 - Maya Chen: Ready for internal beta. Feature flag enabled for platform team. Next steps: console polish, add audit retention policy, finalize security review, prepare rollout playbook. PR #789 updated with server tests and integration harness.
notes: Trade-offs considered: server-side enforcement increases surface but centralizes audit and makes client simpler; client-side schema validation reduces round trips but cannot substitute for server policy checks. We opted for both: client validation for UX, server validation for security. Performance target: validate policy and return decision in <50ms for cached policies; for cross-service checks we surface a 'pending' state and require explicit confirm. Will iterate on policy cache TTLs during beta.
